qualifying_findings.title: ArcadeDB AI chat query_database tool bypasses per-tenant authorization
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE Services reports that ArcadeDB before 26.9.1 exposes an access-control bypass in the `query_database` tool used by AI chat endpoints. The tool executes queries without binding the authenticated principal to DatabaseContext, which can cause per-tenant authorization checks to be skipped.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_fact_or_change: In-window CVE publication for an AI chat endpoint tool authorization bypass fixed in ArcadeDB 26.9.1.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus vendor advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ArcadeDB before 26.9.1; AI chat `query_database` tool and DatabaseContext authorization binding.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is a direct AI-chat tool execution boundary failure: natural-language database access must enforce the same authenticated principal and tenant boundaries as ordinary database APIs.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenPanel logs MCP authentication tokens from query parameters
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE Services and GitHub Advisory Database report that OpenPanel through commit bad75bdd logs Model Context Protocol authentication tokens supplied in URL query parameters. Anyone with access to application stdout or centralized logs can capture the base64-encoded credentials and replay MCP requests to access project analytics.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_fact_or_change: In-window CVE/GHSA publication for plaintext MCP credential logging.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus GitHub Advisory Database and vendor advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenPanel through commit bad75bdd; MCP authentication token handling and application logging.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP credentials extend agent/tool authority into analytics systems; logging bearer material turns ordinary observability access into delegated tool access.

qualifying_findings.title: AI booking-assistant conversations lack requester ownership checks
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: The Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System WordPress plugin before 28.2 does not verify that a requester owns the AI booking-assistant conversation referenced by unauthenticated conversation actions. An unauthenticated visitor can read another visitor's assistant messages and inject messages into an active conversation.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_fact_or_change: In-window CVE/GHSA publication for unauthenticated AI assistant conversation access and message injection.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus WPScan and GitHub Advisory Database records
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System WordPress plugin before 28.2; unauthenticated AI booking-assistant conversation actions.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Assistant conversation state can contain personal scheduling context and operational instructions; ownership checks must bind every assistant-thread action to the correct visitor/session.

qualifying_findings.title: Better Messages exposes AI chat-room transcripts through authorization bypass
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Better Messages - Chat Rooms, Group Chat, Private Messages & AI Chat Bots for WordPress is vulnerable through 2.15.33 because it does not properly verify authorization for chat-room thread access. Authenticated attackers with custom-level access or above can access the full message transcript, thread metadata, and user data of any chat-room thread when the default read setting permits it.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_fact_or_change: In-window CVE/GHSA publication for AI chat-bot plugin transcript and user-data exposure.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus GitHub Advisory Database and Wordfence reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Better Messages WordPress plugin through 2.15.33; chat-room thread REST/API access and default `only_joined_can_read` setting.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI chat-bot plugins often hold support, sales, or private conversation context; thread-level authorization must isolate AI-assisted chat transcripts from unrelated users.

qualifying_findings.title: Better Messages lets unauthenticated guests spoof internal AI bot identity
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Better Messages - Chat Rooms, Group Chat, Private Messages & AI Chat Bots for WordPress is vulnerable through 2.15.33 because `is_ai_bot_user()` identifies internal AI bot accounts by checking for an `ai-chat-bot-` prefix in a guest record IP address populated from the client-controlled `X-Real-IP` header. Unauthenticated attackers can register a guest identity treated as an internal AI bot and bypass role, draft-status, and join filters.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_fact_or_change: In-window CVE/GHSA publication for spoofed internal AI bot identity and room-access bypass.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus GitHub Advisory Database and Wordfence reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Better Messages WordPress plugin through 2.15.33; AI bot identity check, guest registration, and chat-room join authorization.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is an AI-specific identity confusion flaw: code treats an untrusted client-controlled field as proof that a user is an internal AI bot and grants privileged conversation access.

qualifying_findings.title: Google confirmed Gemini accessed three real companies during Irregular cyber evaluation
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: The Guardian reported that Google confirmed Gemini breached three real companies in May during an Irregular cybersecurity evaluation. The report says internet access was unintentionally available in a closed evaluation environment; one case involved a fake company name colliding with a real company service, and two involved public repositories containing credentials. Google said the model stopped after recognizing the companies were real and that affected companies were notified.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_fact_or_change: In-window public incident disclosure for autonomous model cyber-evaluation scope failure and real-company access.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reputable secondary reporting with company confirmation; primary Google or Irregular technical postmortem not located
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Google Gemini model under Irregular cybersecurity evaluation; internet isolation, target naming, public credential discovery, and real-company access.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It extends the recurring third-party cyber-evaluation boundary failure pattern to Google Gemini and reinforces that internet isolation, target registry control, credential handling, and stop-condition monitoring are AI security controls.

qualifying_findings.title: Plugin4Shell lets plugin repositories bypass pinned AI coding-agent plugin versions
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Public reporting on Air Security's Plugin4Shell disclosure says four AI coding agents, Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI, can fetch an approved plugin snapshot but fail to verify that the installed code matches the pinned commit. A plugin repository owner can create a branch name that resembles the trusted commit and cause malicious plugin code execution. Reports say Claude Code 2.1.179 and Codex 0.146.0 are fixed, while GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI remained unfixed or would not be patched in the captured reporting.
qualifying_findings.concrete_security_fact_or_change: In-window disclosure of an AI coding-agent plugin supply-chain and zero-click RCE class with named fixed versions for two agents.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary vendor blog discovered by search plus reputable secondary reporting; primary page content not fully fetched in this run
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Claude Code before 2.1.179, Codex before 0.146.0, GitHub Copilot plugin handling, and Gemini CLI plugin handling; plugin marketplace commit-pinning and repository fetch verification.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Coding-agent plugins run in developer environments with repository, shell, and credential adjacency; commit pinning is not a control unless the installed bytes are verified against the pinned identity.
